title: Distribution of oblique counts across all 13+ trillion closed knight's tours (8×8)

problemStatement.formal: Define `obliqueDistribution : ℕ → ℕ` mapping `k` to the count of closed knight's tours on the 8×8 chessboard with exactly `k` oblique (turn-angle > 90°) turns. Establish structural lemmas (support bounds, D4-orbit divisibility, reversal-symmetry parity, winding-parity constraint) derivable from `Proofs/KnightsTourOblique.lean`'s existing infrastructure (`obliqueCount`, `tour_winding_zero`, `no_turn_angle_4_all`), without enumerating the ~1.3 × 10^13 tours.
problemStatement.plain: Knuth (2025 Christmas Lecture) proved that every closed knight's tour on the 8×8 board has at least 4 oblique turns, and that exactly one tour (up to D4 symmetry) achieves this minimum. This open question asks for the full distribution: how many tours have exactly 5, 6, 7, ... oblique turns? Computing the histogram requires enumerating the 1.3 × 10^13 tours — not feasible in Lean. But the *structural* properties of the distribution — support bounds, D4 invariance, reversal symmetry, winding-parity — are reachable and form the natural Lean deliverable.
whyMatters: Distinguishes structural symmetries of the tour distribution (D4 group action, reversal involution, winding-mod-8 constraint) from its concrete histogram values. The structural skeleton is the Lean-tractable part.

Provides a non-enumerative parametric framework: results stated in terms of `Fintype.card ClosedTour` rather than the concrete value 13,267,364,410,532, avoiding the need for an axiom-tagged total count.

Closes a follow-up question to the parent gallery's minimum theorem. The OQ-02 deliverable extends the gallery in the same direction OQ-01 did (n×n generalization) but along a different axis (distribution refinement at fixed n=8).

Surfaces a `Fintype ClosedTour` infrastructure gap in the parent file. The parent uses `Classical.choice` to express tours; OQ-02 needs an explicit `Fintype` to define the distribution as a `Finset.filter` count.

proven: Minimum oblique count = 4 (8×8): `KnightsTourOblique.lean` plus axiom `knuth_unique_four_oblique` for uniqueness up to D4.
open: Support lemma `obliqueDistribution k = 0 for k < 4` (Target B, S2).
D4 group action on `ClosedTour` + `obliqueCount`-invariance (Target C, S3).
Reversal symmetry: `obliqueCount (reverse t) = obliqueCount t` (Target D, S3).
Winding-parity constraint on joint distribution of `#turnAngle = 3` and `#turnAngle = 5` (Target E, S4).
Better support upper bound `obliqueDistribution k = 0 for k > K` (Target F, optional).
knownResults.goal: Build the structural skeleton of the oblique-count distribution — support, D4-mod-8, reversal-mod-2, winding-parity — derivable from the existing infrastructure in `KnightsTourOblique.lean` without enumeration.

insights: The full histogram is unreachable in Lean (1.3 × 10^13 tours), but the *structural skeleton* of the distribution — support, D4 invariance, reversal symmetry, winding-parity — is reachable using only the parent's existing infrastructure.

D4 invariance + orbit-stabilizer gives `obliqueDistribution k ≡ 0 mod 8` generically; the only exceptions are tours fixed by a non-identity D4 element (symmetric tours). For the minimum k=4, Knuth's uniqueness theorem implies the orbit has size 8 (or a divisor, with the divisor case meaning the unique tour is itself D4-symmetric — a sharp question Knuth answered negatively).
Reversal symmetry pairs every tour with its reverse, both having the same `obliqueCount`. Generically forces `obliqueDistribution k ≡ 0 mod 2`. Palindromic tours are the exceptions.

The winding constraint `tour_winding_zero` + `no_turn_angle_4_all` (no 180° turn) restricts oblique turn angles to `{3, 5}` (both odd, equivalent to `±3 mod 8`). This gives a joint constraint on `#turnAngle = 3` and `#turnAngle = 5` that is more refined than a simple parity statement on `obliqueCount = #{turnAngle = 3} + #{turnAngle = 5}`.

The parent file uses `Classical.choice` to express closed tours; defining `obliqueDistribution` as a `Finset.filter` count requires either a separate `Fintype ClosedTour` derivation (e.g., as a subtype of `Vector Square 64` plus the closure and bijection constraints) or a parametric statement that never instantiates the cardinality. The parametric route is cleaner.
mathlibGaps: No `Fintype` instance for `ClosedTour` in the parent file. The parent uses `Classical.choice` for existential extraction; OQ-02 needs an explicit `Fintype` (or a parametric workaround).

Mathlib has `MulAction` and `Quotient` for orbit-stabilizer, but no boilerplate D4 module — the D4 group action on `ClosedTour` will need to be built explicitly from horizontal-flip + 90°-rotation generators (8 elements).
Mathlib's `IsCycle` / `Cycle` infrastructure may apply to `ClosedTour`'s cyclic permutation viewpoint; check before re-implementing reversal symmetry.
